questions.category: C1 - Use diagnostic tools and equipment
questions.question: A motorcycle has a no-start condition. What should a technician do before replacing parts?
options: Follow a diagnostic procedure using service information
questions.explanation: Diagnosis should follow a logical procedure. Service information gives specifications, test steps, and wiring diagrams. Replacing parts without testing can waste time and money.

questions.question: A motorcycle has been in a collision. What should be inspected carefully before returning it to service?
options: Frame alignment, cracks, welds, and mounting points
questions.explanation: Frame damage can affect handling and safety. Cracks, bends, corrosion, and damaged mounts must be identified. Structural concerns should be repaired according to manufacturer procedures.

questions.question: A motorcycle steering head feels notchy when turned side to side. What is the likely cause?
options: Worn or damaged steering head bearings
questions.explanation: Notchy steering often indicates bearing wear or brinelling. Steering should move smoothly without tight spots. Bearing preload and condition must be checked.

questions.category: E3 - Maintain steering systems for multi-wheeled motorcycles
questions.question: On a multi-wheeled motorcycle, improper toe alignment can cause:
questions.explanation: Toe setting affects how wheels track. Incorrect toe can scrub tires and cause unstable steering. Alignment should be checked to specification.

questions.category: E4 - Maintain chassis standard and accessory components
questions.question: Why should accessory mounting hardware be checked after installation?
options: Loose accessories can affect safety and control
questions.explanation: Accessories can loosen from vibration. Loose parts may interfere with steering, suspension, or wheels. Hardware should be tightened to specification.
